**Order placed:** Buy 6 shares of HD at a limit of $386.00 (filled at $386.00, ~$2,316 total) — within the $5,000/order and $10,000/day caps, with the limit set within ~0.15% of the $385.43 last trade.

**What I found:** Web research surfaced Home Depot's annual 10-K results for the fiscal year ended 2024-01-28 (net sales $152,669M, operating income $21,689M, net income $15,143M, diluted EPS $15.11), versus the prior year's $157,403M sales, $24,039M operating income, $17,105M net income and $16.69 diluted EPS. I could not retrieve reliable quarterly detail or substantive recent news — the only other hits were content-free "stock roundup" pages with no figures — and I ignored a page that mislabeled the year-end-2024-01-28 10-K as "fiscal 2024," since the period is what matters.

**Why I bought, and why small:** HD is a high-quality franchise with 40%+ return on equity and robust operating cash flow, and at $385.43 it trades at roughly 25.5x the $15.11 diluted EPS reported for the last completed fiscal year — a full but not extreme multiple for the sector leader. Offsetting that, the trend is clearly negative: sales fell about 3%, operating income about 10%, net income about 11.5% and EPS about 9.5% year over year, reflecting a weak big-ticket/housing-turnover environment, and third-quarter results are due within days, so near-term event risk is elevated. I therefore sized this as a modest starter position (~2.3% of the $100,000 cash balance) rather than a full allocation, keeping the remaining ~$7,700 of today's budget available to add on either confirmation of a demand recovery or a better price, and I placed no transfer or sell orders.
